title: The Sahibzade week
hookLine: late December, Sikhs remember all four sons and Mata Gujri, some sleeping on the floor

lines: THE SAME STORY, NIGHT AFTER NIGHT.
cards: In some Sikh homes in late December, the mattress comes off the bed and goes onto the floor. A thin blanket. The heater turned down.
No parties, no sweets. Children who'd normally be counting down to a holiday are told a story instead, the same story, night after night.
It's the week Sikhs remember the Sahibzade, the sons of Guru Gobind Singh, and their grandmother, Mata Gujri.

teach.b: Sahibzade means the sons of the Guru's house, and this week keeps all four together with their grandmother. This path told their stories one by one; today, side by side.
The elder sons, Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh, fell fighting at Chamkaur.

The younger sons, Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, were held with Mata Gujri in the cold tower at Sirhind, refused to give up their faith, and were put to death. Tradition says their grandmother died in the tower.
So the week holds a battlefield and a tower, in the same cold season. At Fatehgarh Sahib the Shaheedi Jor Mela gathers crowds; at home, the week is quieter.
Tradition says that after Chamkaur, alone in the forest of Machhiwara, Guru Gobind Singh composed a short song to the beloved friend, kept in the Dasam Granth.

teach.h: A STRAW BED WITH THE FRIEND.
teach.b: One line says, in paraphrase, that a bed of straw with the friend is good, and living in comfortable homes without him is like living in a furnace.
The Guru, having lost so much, chooses the hard ground with the friend over comfort without him.
Families who sleep on the floor this week aren't punishing themselves.
They're keeping company with a grandmother and two boys in a cold tower, and a father sleeping rough in a forest. For a few nights, comfort steps aside so the memory has room.

how: In late December, Sikhs remember the Sahibzade and Mata Gujri with kirtan, langar and the Shaheedi Jor Mela at Fatehgarh Sahib. Some families keep the week simply at home: no celebrations, and sleeping on the floor.

games.q: it's late December in a Sikh home. the kids ask why there's no party this week. what does the family do?
o: keep the week simply and tell the Sahibzade's story.
games.why: some families keep it simply, even sleeping on the floor, and tell the story night after night.

practice: Some night this week, if you choose, you might give up one small comfort before sleep, a lighter blanket, no screen in bed, the heater lower, nothing harmful or extreme; for now, just choose which it would be.
Then feel the floor or the chair under you holding you, breathe slowly, and remember the four boys and their grandmother for a minute. If you pray, you can say Waheguru for them.

wordCard.voice: Sahibzade. The sons of the Guru's house, the four sons of Guru Gobind Singh remembered with Mata Gujri in the late-December days some families keep by sleeping simply, on the floor. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: Sahibzade, the sons of the Guru's house.

carryVoice: Your line: the cold week. Four sons and a grandmother, kept together. Stay warm, and see you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Khayal Patshahi 10 ('Mittar pyare nu'): a bed of straw with the friend is good; comfortable homes without him are like a furnace
the deaths of the four Sahibzade at Chamkaur and Sirhind, and Mata Gujri in the cold tower
